key_insight: The paper localizes phase-field fracture computation to a small active crack-tip patch, using Schur complement condensation to avoid solving the full domain at every iteration.
engineering_relevance: This can greatly reduce the cost of large-scale fracture simulations while preserving accurate crack growth predictions, making phase-field methods more practical for engineering analysis.
method: Adaptive mesh refinement and coarsening keeps high resolution near the crack tip.
Inactive exterior subdomains are eliminated with a Schur complement and condensed to the patch interface.
The exterior phase field is frozen and its factorization is reused while the patch stays fixed.
evidence_signal: Across quasi-static, dynamic branching, 3D mixed-mode, and multi-crack tests, the method matches reference solutions with global quantity differences below 0.5% and achieves up to 22.8× wall-time speedup.
watch_item: Accuracy may degrade in the crack wake because the exterior phase field is approximated, and performance depends on how often the active patch changes.
paper_title: Adaptive Crack-Tip Localization of Phase-Field Fracture Computations
